name: Can you put a kitchen in a garage conversion ADU?

mainEntity.name: What are the hardest parts of adding a kitchen to a garage conversion ADU?
mainEntity.text: What are the hardest parts of adding a kitchen to a garage conversion ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: A garage conversion ADU can absolutely include a kitchen, but the kitchen is often the part that exposes the most hidden construction issues. Garages rarely have the plumbing, wiring, insulation, or finished floor heights needed for a real kitchen, so the design has to account for those upgrades from the start. In many cases, the best layout places the kitchen near existing utility access points to reduce trenching and wall openings. Electrical panel capacity is another common issue, especially if the project uses electric cooking, a dishwasher, or multiple small appliances. Many garage conversions also need better moisture control, exhaust ventilation, and floor leveling before finishes go in. Homeowners should expect the kitchen to drive both cost and schedule because it ties together framing, mechanicals, finishes, and inspections. A good contractor will identify these constraints early and design the kitchen around the building’s existing shell instead of trying to force a standard house kitchen into an old garage footprint.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, a garage conversion ADU can include a kitchen, but the hardest parts are usually plumbing, electrical service, insulation, ventilation, and floor-level changes. Existing garages often need new utility routing and upgrades before cabinets and appliances can be installed. Planning the kitchen early prevents expensive rework.
